chapter: Ellington's later years and Quincy Jones
title: The tour after the show closed and the band's lack of style
summary: When the show closed in Paris the band toured Europe with Nat Cole and the Platters, returned to no bookings, and lacked a distinct style.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And so the show closed when we got to Paris, so Quincy asked the guys in the band if they wanted to stay together. We said sure. So we stayed together. We toured all over Europe. We played the folk parks up in Sweden for the summer and when Nat Cole came over to Europe we did his tour with him. When the Platters came over, the singing group, we did the tour with them. And we just worked over in Paris until that September and we came back. We came back to New York, and when we came back to New York a certain booking agent was supposed to have work for us but that didn't happen. They didn't even know in New York that Quincy had a band, and it was a shame because it was such a good band, such a good band, good music. Quincy made the arrangements. Billy Byers made a lot of the arrangements. Benny Golson had some arrangements in the book. It was a good book.

Only thing that we found out about the band even though it was a good book and everything, there was not enough individual style for you to associate the band with having a style, you see. That was kind -- a little, kind of little bad, too, you see. A band has got to have a style.
